# Phase 3 reconciliation fixtures

What Phase 3 does when an authorized path already exists: `prov-2026-4c49ca46`.

## Layout

Each case directory holds:

| file | |
|---|---|
| `existing` | the file already on disk |
| `template` | its file template **as rendered**, never the template source |
| `expected` | the required bytes back. Absent for a case that halts |

`cases.json` carries each case's `comment_prefix`, its `outcome` — `apply`,
`unchanged` or `halt` — the `diagnostic` a halt must produce, and a `why`.

`comment_prefix` is per case. A comparison reads no language: a line is
structural unless it is blank or starts with the package's declared prefix, and
a new prefix needs a case and nothing else.

## Where the inputs come from

Nothing here is hand-written. `rails-new-routes` is `config/routes.rb` from
`rails _7.2.3_ new --api`; the `rails-generate-*` cases are rendered from
railties' own `controller.rb.tt`. The Go and Cairn inputs are generated by Sedum
from the packages in this repository, then evolved by adding an anchor to the
template and regenerating. Rendered templates come from `grow --stop-after
files`.

## Coverage

| prefix | cases |
|---|---|
| `#` | 11 |
| `//` | 4 |
| `;;` | 2 |

Adoption cases — a file some other tool wrote — are `#` only, because Rails is
the one stack here with a generator to produce authentic input.

## Cases worth reading first

- **`rails-generate-bare` applies, `rails-generate-actions` halts.** The
  boundary is not that controller templates cannot be adopted: an empty
  generated controller adopts exactly, one carrying hand-written actions does
  not.
- **`private-with-method` halts because of the method, not the keyword.**
  `private-empty` is the same file without it, and applies.
- **`evolution-anchor-and-code` and `go-evolution`** are the same situation in
  two languages: an anchor arriving with the code it needs, `private` in Ruby
  and `func init() { }` in Go.

`expected` states required behaviour. Where an implementation disagrees with a
fixture, the fixture is what is right.

## Adding a case

A case is added when a decision is made about what Phase 3 must do, and it
records that decision rather than raising coverage. Real input, or none.

These are internal fixtures rather than a published surface, which is why they
live here and not beside `conformance/`. The marker corpus is published because
a third party writes that format; nothing outside Sedum implements this.
